text:
Adam Engstrom turned 23 this week, and he's spending his first long NHL stretch on the edge of the lineup. He has played 14 games at about 11 and a half minutes a night, sat on Nov. 12 when Mike Matheson drew back in (TSN reported the swap), and was back two nights later.

When he plays, the shot share is good. Montreal has taken 55% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, 5.4 points better than without him. Some of the scoreboard has been kind, though: the Canadiens have scored 4.4 more goals than their chances deserved with him out there, so his on-ice goal numbers flatter him more than the process does.

The path explains the profile. A third-round pick in 2022 (92nd overall), he played two SHL seasons with Rogle and put up 27 points in 66 AHL games for Laval in 2024-25. Evolving-Hockey liked his even-strength offense in a small 196-minute sample last season, and his name surfaced in Darren Dreger's Dylan Larkin trade talk, per NHLTradeRumor.com. For now the thing to watch is simpler: whether he keeps the spot when everyone is healthy.
